name: Sequential Neural Architectures
description: Deepen your knowledge of recurrent mechanisms, hidden state dynamics, and gating structures.

questions.question: How does the hidden state in a standard RNN update at time step t?
options: By averaging the static embeddings of all preceding tokens
By computing a function of the current input and previous hidden state
By applying self-attention weights across the entire sentence
By resetting the activation values back to random uniform noise
questions.explain: The hidden state combines the current input vector with the previous hidden state at each step.

questions.question: What primary computational issue occurs during backpropagation through time in vanilla RNNs?
options: Matrix dimensions shrink dynamically across every layer
Gradients exponentially vanish or explode across deep time steps
Token embeddings lose their assigned semantic vector coordinates
The model converts continuous activations into discrete integers
questions.explain: Repeated matrix multiplications over long temporal steps cause gradients to vanish or explode.

questions.question: Which analogy best illustrates the memory degradation of standard RNNs on long texts?
options: Translating a full document into binary machine code
Shuffling a deck of cards before dealing every round
Reading a book and forgetting the protagonist by chapter two
Looking up every unknown word in a printed dictionary
questions.explain: The slide uses the analogy of reading a book and forgetting early character names as context grows.

questions.question: How does the Cell State in an LSTM facilitate long-range information transfer?
options: It acts as a conveyor belt allowing information to flow unchanged
It applies non-linear pooling to compress the sequence length
It calculates global pairwise cross-attention between tokens
It removes stopwords deterministically prior to inference
questions.explain: The cell state functions like a conveyor belt, preserving key signals across extended steps.

questions.question: Why does training recurrent networks fail to fully utilize modern parallel GPU architectures?
options: Recurrent units require double-precision floating-point CPUs
Step t strictly depends on the sequential output of step t minus one
Backpropagation through time cannot calculate loss gradients
Recurrent layers discard token order during parameter updates
questions.explain: Sequential dependencies prevent simultaneous token computations across multiple GPU cores.

questions.question: What key limitation of Bag-of-Words and LDA was directly solved by RNN sequence modeling?
options: Inability to handle continuous word embeddings
High computational cost of matrix inversion
Inability to account for word order and negation context
Lack of support for unsupervised topic discovery
questions.explain: RNNs process tokens sequentially, distinguishing between phrases with identical words but different meanings.

questions.question: In sequential sentiment analysis, why is order preservation essential for phrases like 'not bad'?
options: Negation tokens invert semantic polarity based on their position
Stopword filters automatically remove positive descriptive words
Word embeddings assign equal vector values to opposing concepts
Classification layers only evaluate the final token in the sequence
questions.explain: Sequential order determines how modifying words like 'not' alter the meaning of surrounding words.

questions.question: How do Word Embeddings complement recurrent layers in deep NLP pipelines?
options: They eliminate the need for temporal hidden state updates
They map words to continuous semantic vectors before recurrence
They enforce strict rule-based syntactic grammar constraints
They convert sentences into sparse high-dimensional count matrices
questions.explain: Dense word embeddings provide semantic vector inputs that the recurrent layers process sequentially.

questions.question: What structural transition marked the evolution from LSTM networks to Transformers?
options: Replacing recurrent connections entirely with attention mechanisms
Increasing the number of recurrent hidden cells per time step
Returning to Bag-of-Words representations for faster training
Removing positional information completely from input sentences
questions.explain: Transformers discarded recurrent recurrence in favor of parallel self-attention mechanisms.

questions.question: Which task represents a sequential classification objective suited for recurrent networks?
options: Clustering unlabelled documents into latent themes
Computing document-wide inverse term frequencies
Categorizing customer reviews as positive or negative
Generating word-level morphological dictionary lemmas
questions.explain: Sentiment classification of customer reviews is a classic supervised task for sequence models.
